html:
In the app

Guided mode’s first lesson is this chapter. It counts the parts you have placed against this list (name, type and position within 10 px) and names the ones still missing or out of place. Place them for me does the whole list in one click when you would rather get to the programming.

File → New Project… → Empty project. Set the floor to 2400 × 600 (Floor on the simulator toolbar) and the view to Top-down. Open the Palette. Place the parts below, then set each one’s position in the Properties drawer (type the numbers; dragging is for later). Names: type them in the name field at the top of Properties; every name here is used by the program, so use them exactly. The mix kitchen at the right of the floor is placed in chapter 30.

Each entry gives the part, its position, its name and the settings that differ from the part’s defaults; anything not listed is left as it comes. The note after it says why.

The main line

  • Emitter at x 60, y 150, named Bottle_Feed: Part to Emit = bottle, bottleL; Min Time (s, continuous / automatic) = 2.5; Max Time (s, continuous / automatic) = 4; Broken bottles (%) = 15. Edge mode: one bottle per rising edge of Emit. Fifteen per cent of them come out broken; that is the scrap the line has to deal with.
  • Belt / Roller / Chain Conveyor at x 80, y 150, named Main_Conv: Length (m), 0.5 to 40 in half-metre steps = 20; Speed (mm/s) = 60; Conveyor type = slat chain; Belt color = Grey; Height (3D) = Raised deck (+1.7 m); Incremental encoder (adds A, B and Pulses) = ticked; Encoder resolution (px per pulse) = 40. Twenty metres of slat chain on a raised deck, with an encoder of 40 px per pulse: one pulse is one stop. The deck is what lets the gates drop bottles to the conveyors below.
  • Diffuse Sensor at x 160, y 150, named LS1: Sensing range (px; 60 px = 1 m) = 14. Bottle present at the head of the line. On the 40 px stop grid, one stop before LS2.
  • Retroreflective Sensor and Reflector at x 200, y 150, named LS2: Beam height (px above the belt) = 48. A retro beam 48 px up: only a large bottle (56 px tall) breaks it; a small one (40 px) passes under.
  • Diffuse Sensor at x 240, y 150, named LS3: Sensing range (px; 60 px = 1 m) = 14; Sees = broken bottles. Set to see broken bottles only.
  • Fill Station at x 440, y 150, named Filler: Fed from = Supply_Tank. Fed from =
  • Inline Cap Feeder at x 560, y 150, named Capper (default settings). Thirty caps in the chute to start; the magazine refills it at 3 caps a second when Feeder runs.
  • Inline Labeler at x 600, y 150, named Labeler: Applicator = Wrap-around (roller); Roll holds (labels) = 200. One stop past the capper. RH, wrap- around roller: the dispenser stands on the far side of the lane; 200 labels on the roll to start.
  • Vision Sensor at x 640, y 150, named Camera: Output = camera tags only; Camera module (its name in I/O Configuration; blank = wired signals only) = Cam1; Inspection job = Bottle inspection (cap, label, fill). The inspection camera of step 15, one stop past the labeler: an In-Sight vision sensor set to its bottle-inspection job (cap, label, fill). Its I/O is the EtherNet/IP module Cam1, which step 15 adds.
  • Process HMI at x 700, y 450, named Cam_HMI: Shows = Camera; Function keys F2–F6: other machines this terminal can switch to (names, comma-separated; F1 is Shows) = Supply_Tank, Mix_Tank, Case_Packer, Bottle_Feed; Screen = 10 inch. The camera’s own terminal beside the line: each result with its picture. Its function keys reach the other machines, so it can stand in for any terminal on the line.
  • Pivot Arm Sorter at x 720, y 150, named Scrap_Gate (default settings). A pivot arm. Its push side is +y, toward the grinder.
  • Pivot Arm Sorter at x 1000, y 150, named Divert_Gate (default settings). Pushes toward the divert conveyor, 166 px below on the lower level.
  • Diffuse Sensor at x 1240, y 150, named LS11: Sees = bottles only. Set to see bottles only. One stop before the end of the line: the program checks here that the bottle it expects at this stop is really there (step 11).

Supply

  • Reservoir at x 300, y 60, named Supply_Tank: Product = Soda; Holds (units; a small bottle takes 60, a large 100) = 2000; Starts at (%) = 35; Inlet flow (units/s) = 150; Low float (%) = 20. Soda, 2000 units, starting at 35 % so you see the inlet work early. High float 90 %, low float 20 %. Leave Inlet fed from on the plant supply header for now: lesson 15 pipes it from the mix kitchen.
  • Stack Light at x 300, y 40, named Tank_Light: Mount = Direct; Built-in flasher = Red flashes. Mounted directly on the tank dome; its red segment flashes when driven.

The lower level

  • Grinder at x 720, y 240, named Grinder (default settings). Placed 90 px below the scrap gate so a bottle pushed off the deck lands in its hopper; its chute reaches the box conveyor 76 px further down.
  • Emitter at x 380, y 320, named Box_Feed: Part to Emit = cartonM; Carton / tote / bottle colour = Y; Mode = automatic (no Emit input); Min Time (s, continuous / automatic) = 4; Max Time (s, continuous / automatic) = 4; Automatic: count the time only while the exit is clear (keeps a gap after a stop) = ticked. A carton every 4 s, by itself.
  • Belt / Roller / Chain Conveyor at x 400, y 320, named Scrap_Conv: Length (m), 0.5 to 40 in half-metre steps = 8; Speed (mm/s) = 80; Conveyor type = roller. The box conveyor, LogixPro's "scrap conveyor". Eight metres of roller.
  • Diffuse Sensor at x 510, y 320, named LS13: Sensing range (px; 60 px = 1 m) = 4; Sees = boxes only. The eye of the hazard-tape dispenser, ten pixels before its head: a box is seen in time for the wipe-on cycle to meet it.
  • Inline Labeler at x 520, y 320, named Haz_Labeler: Hand (side of the lane the dispenser stands on, looking downstream) = LH; What it applies = Hazard tape (scrap boxes); Applicator = Wipe-on (dispensing edge + brush); Apply time (s) = 0.3; Only label capped bottles (skips an open one and logs it) = off. The second labeler, on the far side of the box conveyor (LH), set to hazard tape with a wipe-on applicator: it bands each scrap box yellow and black on its way to the chute. Boxes come off Box_Feed blank.
  • Diffuse Sensor at x 740, y 320, named LS10: Sensing range (px; 60 px = 1 m) = 4; Sees = boxes only. Boxes only, placed so a carton stops centred under the chute.
  • Remover at x 880, y 320, named Box_Out (default settings). At the end of the box conveyor.
  • Belt / Roller / Chain Conveyor at x 960, y 320, named Divert_Conv: Length (m), 0.5 to 40 in half-metre steps = 6; Conveyor type = roller. Starts under the divert gate; the catch incline from the deck lands on it. Six metres: it runs on to the end under the case packer, which picks the small bottles off it.
  • Diffuse Sensor at x 1240, y 320, named LS12: Sensing range (px; 60 px = 1 m) = 14; Sees = bottles only. Bottles only. The stop eye at the end of the divert conveyor, just before the packer's lower lane: when the lane is full, a bottle waiting here stops the conveyor (step 7).

Packing

  • Case Packer at x 1300, y 150, named Case_Packer: Second pick lane below: the head drops to a conveyor on the floor (small bottles) = ticked; Lower lane offset across the line (px; positive = near side) = 170. At the end of the main line: its infeed takes the large bottles off the end of the deck, and its pick head reaches across to the case lane 108 px away on the far side. Tick Second pick lane below with the lower lane 166 px away on the near side: the divert conveyor runs on under the packer, and the head drops 1.7 m to pick the small bottles off its end.
  • Process HMI at x 1130, y 450, named Pack_HMI: Shows = Case_Packer; Function keys F2–F6: other machines this terminal can switch to (names, comma-separated; F1 is Shows) = Supply_Tank, Mix_Tank, Camera, Bottle_Feed; START button tag (BOOL, pulsed while touched) = Pack_Start; STOP button tag (BOOL, pulsed while touched) = Pack_Stop; Running indicator tag (BOOL: lights START) = Pack_Run; Packer: large cases count tag (DINT) = Case_Large_Count; Packer: small cases count tag (DINT) = Case_Small_Count; Screen = 10 inch. The packer’s own terminal, beside it. START, STOP and Running are the packer’s own tags (step 12); the two count tags fill its CASES LARGE and CASES SMALL cards.
  • Belt / Roller / Chain Conveyor at x 1530, y 40, rotation 2°, named Case_Conv: Length (m), 0.5 to 40 in half-metre steps = 4.5; Speed (mm/s) = 150; Driven by drive module (its name; blank = contactor) = Case_VFD; Conveyor type = roller; Height (3D) = Raised deck (+1.7 m). The case lane: a raised roller conveyor running right to left (rotation 180°) past the packer head. Its Driven by drive module is Case_VFD, so it has no Fwd output of its own: the drive runs it.
  • Emitter at x 1550, y 40, rotation 2°, named Case_Feed: Part to Emit = cartonL; Carton / tote / bottle colour = Y; Mode = automatic (no Emit input). An empty carton every 3 s at the upstream (right-hand) end, whenever there is room.
  • Diffuse Sensor at x 1420, y 40, named Case_Slow: Sensing range (px; 60 px = 1 m) = 12; Sees = boxes only. Boxes only, 100 px before the packer head: the slow-down eye.
  • Remover at x 1260, y 40, rotation 2°, named Case_Out (default settings). At the downstream end of the lane: packed cases leave here.
  • VFD at x 1150, y 50, named Case_VFD (default settings). The drive for the case lane: 60 Hz at 10 V, 1 s accel, 0.5 s decel.

The operator console

  • Panel / Enclosure at x 1510, y 350, named Panel_1: Style = Operator console; Width (px) = 280; Height (px) = 340; Title plate (blank for none) = BOTTLE LINE. The console stands at the right-hand end of the line, clear of the packer’s lower lane.
  • Push Button at x 1430, y 250, named Start_PB (default settings). Normally open: its Pressed signal is 1 while it is held.
  • Push Button at x 1490, y 250, named Stop_PB: Color = red; Legend text (Legend button style) = STOP; Normally closed contact = ticked. Normally closed: its Pressed signal is 1 until it is pressed.
  • Indicator Light / LED at x 1560, y 250, named Run_Lamp (default settings). Lit while the line runs (step 1).
  • Indicator Light / LED at x 1620, y 250, named Fault_Lamp: Color = red; Legend text (Legend plate style) = FAULT. Flashes while an alarm is unacknowledged, steady once acknowledged (step 11).
  • Push Button at x 1620, y 320, named Reset_PB: Color = blue; Legend text (Legend button style) = RESET. Acknowledges alarms and clears those whose cause has gone (step 11).
  • Selector Switch at x 1410, y 320, named Carb_Key: Handle = Key; Starts in the right-hand position = ticked. The carbonation key: turned to ON, the kitchen may carbonate (step 13).
  • Indicator Light / LED at x 1630, y 390, named Carb_Lamp: Color = amber; Legend text (Legend plate style) = CO2. The amber lamp beside the key: carbonation enabled.
  • Thumbwheel Switch at x 1510, y 320, named Preset_TW (default settings). The batch preset: the line stops itself at this many large bottles; Enter clears the counts (step 9).
  • Digital Display at x 1450, y 390, named Small_Disp: Tag to show (blank = the wired analog output) = Small_Bottle_Count; Width (characters) = 4; Digit color = amber; Caption on the bezel (optional) = SMALL. Shows the tag named in its settings; the tag does not exist yet, so the display reads dashes until chapter 17.
  • Digital Display at x 1570, y 390, named Large_Disp: Tag to show (blank = the wired analog output) = Large_Bottle_Count; Width (characters) = 4; Digit color = amber; Caption on the bezel (optional) = LARGE.
  • Digital Display at x 1450, y 440, named Scrap_Disp: Tag to show (blank = the wired analog output) = Scrap_Bottle_Count; Width (characters) = 4; Digit color = amber; Caption on the bezel (optional) = SCRAP.
  • Digital Display at x 1570, y 440, named Box_Disp: Tag to show (blank = the wired analog output) = Scrap_Box_Count; Width (characters) = 4; Digit color = amber; Caption on the bezel (optional) = BOXES.
  • Digital Display at x 1450, y 490, named Box_Level_Disp: Tag to show (blank = the wired analog output) = Box_Level; Width (characters) = 2; Caption on the bezel (optional) = IN BOX. The bottles in the box under the chute, read from the grinder.
  • Digital Display at x 1570, y 490, named Case_Disp: Tag to show (blank = the wired analog output) = Case_Count; Width (characters) = 4; Digit color = amber; Caption on the bezel (optional) = CASES. CASES: the case count from step 12.

That is 46 parts. Their signals take 63 digital inputs, 33 digital outputs, 8 analog inputs and 1 analog output; the Scene sheet (click empty floor, Properties) counts what is in use. Switch to Side view and then 3D and walk along it: the pipe from the tank to the filler draws itself, the incline from the deck lands on the divert conveyor, the gates have their doors.

Run it with no program

Go to Run mode. Nothing moves, because every output is off; but the feeders set to automatic are not outputs: boxes start arriving on the box conveyor and queue at its head, because the conveyor is not running either, and cases do the same on the case lane. Back to Program mode.

Watch for

Positions are the centre of a conveyor’s start and the centre of every other part. A sensor must be on the conveyor’s centreline (y = 150 on the main line) to see bottles; a station must be at a stop position (x = 160 + 40n) to meet a bottle standing still. If you place by dragging, the snap does both for you.
